The merge wizard's two were one defect: _process_query took `SQL | str` and
re-wrapped a str at the call site, so a raw string reached the cursor through a
parameter. addons/product/wizard/product_merge.py -- the same wizard, one tree
over -- already takes `SQL` and suppresses its execute with a rationale. base now
matches it exactly: the signature is `SQL`, parent_migration_process_cb wraps its
own literal, and the execute carries the same '# noqa: E8501  built by
_generate_query'.

ir_model_common's cast built a type name with SQL() when SQL.identifier() is the
constructor for a name. Verified rather than assumed: every value column_type[0]
can take -- int4, int8, float8, numeric, bool, varchar, text, date, timestamp,
jsonb -- casts correctly when quoted (SELECT 1::"int4", now()::"timestamp", ...).

ir_module's _dependency_closure takes the query as a parameter, which the checker
cannot see through; both callers pass a module-level constant and nothing else
does, so the execute names them in its rationale.

Control run at 3bbd93238b3 with none of my files applied reports 33 against a
floor of 35, so 2 of this fall predate the change.
